Snakemake: file-based workflows for Python and anything else

The problem it solves

A model project is a chain: prepare the data, fit the model, make predictions, draw the plot. Run by hand, the chain breaks in the usual ways. You forget a step, you rerun a slow fit that did not need to run, or you change the preprocessing and keep looking at old predictions.

The general idea

Snakemake is a workflow engine. You write rules: each rule says which files it needs, which files it produces and how to make them. Snakemake builds the dependency graph from those files, runs the rules in the right order, in parallel when it can, and next time only reruns the rules whose inputs changed. A rule can run a shell command, a Python script or an R script, so one workflow can mix languages.

Examples

configfile: "config/config.yaml"
model = config["model"]

rule all:
    input: "output/scenario_estimation.png"

rule preprocess:
    input:  "data/raw/data.xlsx"
    output: "data/process/model_input.json"
    script: "preprocess.py"

rule fit:
    input:  f"models/{model}.stan", "data/process/model_input.json"
    output: f"output/{model}/summary.json"
    script: "fit.py"

rule visualize:
    input:  f"output/{model}/summary.json"
    output: "output/scenario_estimation.png"
    script: "plot.R"
snakemake --cores 4        # run what is outdated
snakemake -n               # dry run: what would run?
snakemake --dag | dot -Tpng > dag.png

Tips from my setup

  • Python scripts run through uv, so every rule uses the project environment. See the post about uv.
  • Mixed languages in one workflow. In my model project the data preparation, the Stan fit and the predictions are Python, and the last rule draws the plot in R.
  • The model is a config value. A config.yaml picks the Stan model, so comparing two models is one changed line.
  • It tells me when it is done. The onsuccess and onerror hooks send a push notification, so a long run on the computer at home does not need watching.
  • Why I moved on. Snakemake decides what is outdated from the files. It does not track parameters or experiments, and my data lives outside git. DVC does both, so new projects start with DVC. See the posts about DVC and dvcat.
